description: Shared golden vectors for search tokenization. Asserted by Go (functions/loans/test/utils/search) and Dart (apps/loans/test/features/search). If the two implementations disagree, search breaks invisibly - no error, a client simply cannot be found - so any change here must be made in both places in the same PR. This file is meant to be sufficient on its own: everything a reimplementation needs is in 'limits' and 'paths' below, not only in the Go source.

schema.case.name: What the case pins. Purely documentation.
schema.case.path: Which function produces the tokens. See paths below. A case with an unknown or missing path is a test failure, not a skip.
schema.case.input: Arguments to that function, in order.
schema.case.tokens: The exact expected output: deduplicated and sorted ascending. Compare as an ordered list.
schema.limits: The numeric bounds every path obeys. These are contract values, not tuning knobs - a reimplementation must use exactly these numbers.
schema.paths: One entry per producer, describing it completely enough to reimplement. 'tokenize' additionally carries the two rules that apply everywhere: normalization and the token cap.

paths.tokenize: Tokenize(input...) - the general tokenizer, applied to name and email fields. Normalizes each value, emits the full normalized value as its own token (exempt from max_prefix, truncated only past max_full_value runes, which no real value reaches), and prefix-expands every word - and every non-alphanumeric-split sub-word - to lengths min_prefix..max_prefix. Words shorter than min_prefix are indexed whole.
paths.tokenize.normalization: Normalization lowercases, folds diacritics, trims the ends, AND collapses every internal run of whitespace to a single space. Collapsing, not merely trimming: 'Juan  Carlos' (double space, an ordinary paste artefact) and 'Juan Carlos' must produce identical token sets, including the same full-value token 'juan carlos'. An implementation that only trims the ends passes every single-word case here and fails the double-space cases - which is exactly why they exist.
paths.tokenize.token_cap: Token cap, in one sentence: one composition prefix-expands only the first max_words whitespace-separated words of its values taken in order - every non-empty value still contributes its full-value token regardless of the budget - and the final sorted list is truncated to its first max_tokens entries. This is not cosmetic: each token costs one index entry per composite index containing search_tokens plus two automatic single-field entries, and Firestore rejects any write exceeding 40,000 index entries for one document, which would make that document permanently unwritable.
paths.phone_tokens: PhoneTokens(input[0]) - mobile numbers only. Takes exactly one input. Strips non-digits, then repeatedly trims a leading 63 or 0 until neither remains, then prefix-expands the canonical form and emits its last 4 digits as a discrete token. Never route a phone number through 'tokenize': it does none of that.
paths.user_tokens: UserTokens(input[0..4]) = first_name, middle_name, last_name, mobile_number, email_address, in that order. Takes exactly five inputs. The four name/email fields are passed to 'tokenize' as a single call (so they share one max_words budget); mobile_number goes through 'phone_tokens'; the two sets are unioned, sorted, and capped at max_tokens. Sending mobile_number through 'tokenize' instead is the specific drift this path exists to catch - it would index 0917... and +63917... as two different clients and silently break phone search.
paths.product_view_tokens: ProductViewTokens(input[0..2]) = company_name, loan_type, tag_line, in that order. Takes exactly three inputs, all passed to 'tokenize' as a single call, so they share one max_words budget. product_views has no product-name field; loan_type carries that meaning, because the add-product flow offers presets plus an 'Others' branch where the lender types free text - which is also why the token cap matters most here.

cases.name: two-letter surname is indexed whole (below the 2-char prefix floor)
simple name expands to prefixes from length 2
apostrophe yields the joined form, the split parts, and the full value
hyphen yields the joined form, the split parts, and the full value
long token: prefixes stop at 12 characters, full value is still emitted whole
multi-word surname: each word is expanded separately and the full value keeps its single space - every real last_name of this shape ('dela Cruz', 'de los Santos') depends on it
multi-word spelling 2 of 2: double space - must equal spelling 1 exactly, because normalization collapses internal whitespace runs rather than only trimming the ends
three-word company name: no joined-across-words token is emitted, only per-word prefixes plus the whole value
phone spelling 2 of 3: E.164 with +63 - must equal spelling 1 exactly
phone spelling 3 of 3: country code without + - must equal spellings 1 and 2 exactly
phone: international access code stacks 0 and 63 - trimming each prefix once instead of looping leaves 0639175550142 or 639175550142 and produces a different token set
full email: pasted address matches exactly, and every part is searchable; the joined form is capped at 12 while the full value is not
users composition: name fields and email go through tokenize, mobile through phone_tokens - note 0917, 555 and 0917 555-0142 are absent, which is what proves the routing
users composition, E.164 mobile with spaces - must equal the previous case exactly; if it does not, the same client is findable by one spelling of their own number and not the other
product_views composition: all three fields through tokenize, each keeping its own full-value token; the double-space tag_line collapses like every other value
